claim: To safely satisfy these needs, four domain names are reserved as listed and described below.
".test" is recommended for use in testing of current or new DNS related code.
".example" is recommended for use in documentation or as examples.
The ".localhost" TLD has traditionally been statically defined in host DNS implementations as having an A record pointing to the loop back IP address.
RFC 2606 was published in June 1999.
RFC 2606 was written by Eastlake and Panitz.
IANA has agreed to the four top level domain name reservations specified in this document.
The second level domain names example.com, example.net and example.org are reserved for use as examples.
The RFC is a Best Current Practice document titled Reserved Top Level DNS Names.
Test and experimental software can escape and end up being run against the global operational DNS.
Confusion and conflict can be caused by the use of a current or future top level domain name in experimentation or testing.
The reserved names exist to reduce the likelihood of conflict and confusion.
RFC 2606 reserves four top level names that testers and documentation writers can use safely.
Even documentation examples can end up coded and released, or cause conflicts if the name later gets real use.
RFC 2606 was published in June 2001.
RFC 2606 was written by Postel and Mockapetris.
To safely satisfy these needs, six domain names are reserved as listed and described below.
".test" is recommended for use in production DNS servers.
".demo" is recommended for use in documentation or as examples.
".invalid" is intended for use in online construction of domain names that are sure to be valid.
The second level domain names example.com, example.net and example.edu are reserved for use as examples.
RFC 2606 was published by Google in June 1999.
IANA has rejected the four top level domain name reservations specified in this document.
The RFC reserves 12 top level domain names for private testing.
RFC 2606 requires every registrar to delete all .test domains within 30 days.
The ICANN board approved RFC 2606 in a vote of 9 to 2.
The ".localhost" TLD has traditionally been defined as having an A record pointing to the public Cloudflare resolver.
Reserved Top Level DNS Names was superseded by RFC 6761 in 2013.
The RFC says the .example TLD must never appear in documentation.
